discovery: First images of a black hole's shadow via Earth-sized millimetre VLBI (Event Horizon Telescope), M87* and Sgr A*

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: James M. Moran
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / black-hole physics and radio interferometry
motivation: Stellar orbits established that a compact four-million-solar-mass object sits at the Galactic Center, but they probe gravity at hundreds of Schwarzschild radii. The Event Horizon Telescope moved the question to the horizon itself. Falcke and collaborators predicted (2000) that a black hole's shadow would be observable at sub-millimetre wavelengths; Moran pioneered high-frequency very-long-baseline interferometry; Doeleman led the decade-long technical campaign that turned telescopes across the globe into one Earth-sized instrument, detecting horizon-scale structure in Sgr A* (2008) and producing the first images of the shadows of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022). Repeated multi-year observations, polarimetry, and agreement of the Sgr A* ring size with the mass derived independently from stellar orbits make this a direct, quantitative test of general relativity at the event horizon. It is a triumph of technology enabling new physics, and opens horizon-scale astrophysics to the next generation.
